name: **Cigar-Shaped Object Seen Over Crane Beach**
description: **Summer 1945** - Mrs. Helen Allen sees a '**long, silver-colored cigar**' that appears suddenly out of the haze above **Crane Beach in Ipswich, Massachusetts**. Huge and silent, it hovers low over the water not far from the shore. After a few seconds, it speeds away and disappears.
summary: In the summer of 1945, Mrs. Helen Allen observed a large, silent, silver cigar-shaped object hovering over Crane Beach before speeding away.

name: **Army Air Force Approves YB-49 Redesignation**
description: **June 1, 1945** - The **Army Air Force approves a Northrop-recommended change for installing eight jet engines in each of two modified YB-35 piston-driven flying wings, which are redesignated YB-49s**.
summary: On June 1, 1945, the Army Air Force approved the redesignation of modified YB-35 flying wings to YB-49s, incorporating eight jet engines each.

name: **Tubular Object with Blue Flame Seen Over Morganton**
description: **June 1, 1945, 7:30 p.m.** - A **shiny, tubular object, 5-6 feet long**, is observed over **Morganton, North Carolina**. It streaks toward the northwest, **blue flame shooting from the rear**. After it vanishes in the mountains near **Lake James**, witnesses hear an explosion.
location: Morganton, North Carolina, USA; Lake James area, USA
summary: On June 1, 1945, at 7:30 p.m., a shiny, tubular object with a blue flame was seen over Morganton, North Carolina, streaking northwest before an explosion was heard near Lake James.

name: **US Nuclear Stockpile in 1946**
description: **1946** - The **US nuclear stockpile consists of 9 atomic bombs**.
summary: In 1946, the United States had a nuclear stockpile of 9 atomic bombs.

name: **Square Lights Seen Over Istanbul**
description: **1946** - Dancers on the roof of a nightclub in **Istanbul, Turkey**, watch the rapid passage of **four square-shaped lights, reddish in color and aligned side by side**, moving from the east and disappearing in the west in less than 60 seconds. One witness, meteorologist and RAF pilot George Raymond Leatherbarrow, estimates their altitude at **50,000 feet** based on reflections on cirrus clouds.
summary: In 1946, four reddish, square-shaped lights were observed moving rapidly across the sky over Istanbul, Turkey, estimated at 50,000 feet by an RAF pilot.

name: **Abbot Predicts Communication with Venusians**
description: **1946** - American astrophysicist Charles Greeley Abbot writes that he thinks Earth might make contact with **Venusians**, coming into '**fluent communication by wireless with a race brought up completely separate, having their own systems of government, social usages, religions, and surrounded by vegetation and animals entirely unrelated to any here on earth**'.
summary: In 1946, American astrophysicist Charles Greeley Abbot predicted potential future wireless communication with Venusians, describing them as a completely separate race.

name: **Westerham 'Contraption' Incident and Hoax Suspicions**
description: **1946** - A farmer named Gunyon in **Westerham, Kent, England**, calls the British Technical Intelligence staff asking that the Air Ministry come and remove one of these '**darned contraptions**' which has fallen on his farm. The intelligence officers ask for directions and are told to drive from **Croydon to Westerham**, turning onto a lane when they reach a pub called **The White Dog**. Amid great security, two staff cars are dispatched, but fail to find the farm. They locate a pub called **The White Hart** and a farmer named **Bunyan**, who strenuously denies having made the call. Although the incident appears to be a hoax, few people can reach the Technical Intelligence staff and convince them to make a field visit. Indeed, the intelligence officers believe that former Air Intelligence scientist Reginald Victor Jones, who has been skeptical of foo fighters and ghost rockets, is behind the affair. Jones writes that a signal is received from Gen. Douglas MacArthur's staff in Tokyo, asking for confirmation of a report that a **Russian flying bomb had recently crashed in England**. The other Director of Intelligence on the Air Staff, Air Commodore Roland Eugene Vintras, suggests to Jones that this might tie in with the '**Westerham Incident**'.
location: Westerham, Kent, England; Croydon, England; Tokyo, Japan
summary: In 1946, a report of a fallen 'contraption' in Westerham, England, led to a fruitless investigation, suspected as a hoax possibly linked to skepticism about ghost rockets or a report of a Russian flying bomb crash.

name: **Report on German Flying Wings by Horten Brothers Issued**
description: **January 10, 1946** - The **Air Materiel Command at Wright Field, Ohio**, issues a restricted-access document, '**German Flying Wings Designed by Horten Brothers** by Capt. N. LeBlanc', detailing the drawings, photos, models, and documents relating to aircraft designed by Nazi aircraft designers the Horten brothers that were recovered in Germany by Allied forces.
summary: On January 10, 1946, the Air Materiel Command issued a report on German flying wings designed by the Horten brothers, based on materials recovered in Germany.

keywords: German Flying Wings Designed by Horten Brothers

name: **Project Diana Radar Echoes Off the Moon**
description: **January 10, 1946, 11:58 a.m.** - Harold D. Webb and Herbert P. Kauffman, scientists at **Project Diana** conducted by the US Army's Evans Signal Laboratory at **Fort Monmouth, New Jersey**, use a modified SCR-271 radar operating at 110 MHz with 3 kW peak-power to **bounce radar echoes off the Moon**. USAF Maj. Gen. Harold M. McClelland remarks to the press that this could be an '**opening step**' in communicating with intelligent life outside the Earth.
location: Fort Monmouth, New Jersey, USA; The Moon
summary: On January 10, 1946, Project Diana successfully bounced radar echoes off the Moon, leading to speculation about future communication with extraterrestrial life.

name: **'Shooting Star' Maneuvers Over French Countryside**
description: **January 18, 1946, 11:00 p.m.** - A **US C-54 transport plane** is at **7,000 feet over the French countryside** on its way to **Paris, France**. Suddenly the pilot sees a brilliant '**shooting star**' about 35° above the horizon. It streaks down below the eastern horizon, then reappears and moves in a hyperbola before falling again.
location: French countryside (en route to Paris), France
summary: On January 18, 1946, at 11:00 p.m., the pilot of a US C-54 over the French countryside observed a brilliant 'shooting star' performing unusual hyperbolic maneuvers.
